reason: E1 shows that O and N cause phase segregation and softening in a TiVNbTa RHEA, supporting the first two premises. However, E1 does not demonstrate that reducing impurities suppresses segregation or improves strength, nor does it involve Ni-containing alloys; the cited evidence is only loosely related to the proposed intervention and predicted outcome.
premises: Trace oxygen and nitrogen impurities promote phase segregation during elevated-temperature exposure in HEAs containing Ti.
Impurity-induced phase segregation depletes the matrix of solutes, causing softening.
Reducing impurities via ultra-high purity melting suppresses phase segregation.
Suppressing segregation preserves solid solution strengthening and enhances high-temperature yield strength.
